title: Tribal Movements Chuar Uprising
definition: The Chuar Uprising was a series of agrarian-tribal revolts (1766–1816) led by the Bhumij and other tribal groups against the British East India Company's oppressive land revenue policies and the displacement of traditional tribal landholders in the Jungle Mahals region.
importanceInUpsc: It represents the earliest phase of tribal resistance against colonial land revenue systems (Permanent Settlement) and the erosion of traditional tribal autonomy, frequently appearing in Prelims regarding chronology and causes.
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Tribal Movements Chuar Uprising.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
